purpose: Click is a Python library for building command-line interfaces. You compose commands, groups, options and arguments with decorators. It generates help, parses and converts arguments, prompts the user, shows progress bars, and provides shell completion and a test runner.
intended_users: Python developers who write CLI tools. Libraries such as Flask build on it. Pallets maintainers and contributors are the other group.
dependencies: Runtime: none declared in pyproject.toml. No [project].dependencies key was seen, so it relies on the standard library; Windows console support is in _winconsole.py
Dependency groups: dev (ruff, tox, tox-uv); tests (pytest); tests-random (pytest, pytest-randomly, pytest-xdist); typing (mypy, pyright, pytest); docs (sphinx and plugins); pre-commit; gha-update

execution_flow: The user calls the command object, or Command.main(), which is core.py:1483. main() takes args from sys.argv[1:], expanding them on Windows, and detects the program name. self._main_shell_completion handles any completion request and exits early. Then make_context builds a Context and calls Command.parse_args, which uses the parser and each Parameter's handle_parse_result. That step resolves the value from the command line, an environment variable, a default map or the default, then runs process_value to convert and validate it. Command.invoke runs the callback. A Group.invoke resolves the subcommand through resolve_command, makes a sub-context and invokes it. In standalone mode, main() catches Exit, Abort, KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError, ClickException and EPIPE OSError. It prints the message and calls sys.exit. With standalone_mode=False it returns the value or propagates the exception.
test_runner: pytest. Config is in pyproject.toml: testpaths=tests, filterwarnings=error, and stress tests excluded by default via addopts.
test_conventions: Files are named test_<topic>.py. Larger areas become packages: tests/test_types, tests/test_utils and tests/test_exceptions, with one file per class or function, e.g. test_Choice.py.
The shared fixture `runner` in tests/conftest.py returns CliRunner() with function scope.
Warnings are turned into errors (filterwarnings=error), so tests that expect a warning must catch it explicitly.
Stress tests carry @pytest.mark.stress and are run only via `tox -e stress`.
Static typing checks run on tests/typing/typing_*.py with mypy and pyright, not pytest.
I did not read individual tests, so assertion style is not documented here.

compatibility_rules.claim: The public API is whatever src/click/__init__.py re-exports with `as` aliases. Internals use underscore prefixes (_compat, _termui_impl, _utils, _winconsole).
Deprecations keep the old name alive through a module-level __getattr__. It emits DeprecationWarning with stacklevel=2 and a message naming the removal version (Click 9.0, or 9.1 for __version__).
The Python floor is 3.10, and the type checkers target 3.10.
Warnings fail the tests, and stress tests are excluded by default.
Typing is strict. The package ships py.typed (src/click/py.typed). mypy runs in strict mode on src and tests/typing, and pyright runs --verifytypes.
The ruff config requires `typing` imported as `t` and single-line imports.
Docstrings carry versionchanged and versionadded notes. CHANGES.md uses a per-version bullet list with {pr} and {issue} references.
Contributor rules: avoid ternary expressions because coverage cannot measure both branches. Avoid unnecessary dependencies, preferring the standard library. Wrap Markdown at 80 columns.
The command-level `deprecated` parameter accepts a bool or a str.
